name: walkthrough
title: Handoff protocols: claims, stale claims, and a handoff skill
description: This tour walks through the handoff protocol tutorial: the claim race using atomic rename, the .claim and .notes files, the stale claim takeover with a time threshold, the finish action, and the trace log. Then it compares atomic rename against check-then-act in a concurrent race.

steps.description: Setup: ROOT folder handoff-demo, three subfolders inbox, claimed, done under handoff/, trace file .ai/trace.jsonl. All directories created fresh.
STALE_AFTER = 300 seconds idle before a claim may be broken. TRACE_ID identifies the session.
log_action writes one JSON line per action to trace.jsonl with timestamp, trace_id, agent, action, task, rule, and extra fields. Never stores prompt text.
post_task writes a task file into inbox/.

claim(agent, name) uses os.rename to move task from inbox/ to claimed/. Atomic on one disk: one caller wins. On FileNotFoundError, logs skip and returns False. On success, writes .claim JSON with claimed_by and claimed_at, logs claim, returns True.
note(agent, name, text) appends to .notes file with agent prefix and timestamp. Each write is a sign of life.
last_write(name) reads .claim JSON and .notes mtime, returns the claim dict and the newest timestamp (claim or notes).

take_if_stale(agent, name) checks if claim is stale: if same agent or idle < STALE_AFTER, logs wait and returns False. Otherwise overwrites .claim with new agent and taken_from, logs break-claim, returns True.
finish(agent, name, result) moves task from claimed/ to done/, removes .claim, moves .notes to done/, writes .result.md with finished_by and result, logs finish.
show() prints contents of inbox/, claimed/, done/.

Demo sequence: post task-7.md, A claims (True), B claims (False), A notes, B tries take too early (False), show state. Then simulate A dying: backdate claim and notes by STALE_AFTER+1. B takes stale claim (True), B finishes, show final state.

steps.description: Idle exceeds STALE_AFTER, take_if_stale overwrites .claim with agent-B and taken_from agent-A, logs break-claim with idle_s and taken_from, returns True.
Move to the race comparison.
rename_claim uses a single os.rename. It either happens or it does not. No intermediate state.
check_then_act_claim checks os.path.exists, reads the file, sleeps, then writes and removes. Two steps with a gap where anything can happen.

race(claim_fn, rounds=100) creates a temp folder with one task file, uses a Barrier to release two threads at the same instant, runs claim_fn for each agent, counts rounds where both agents win (double claim).

steps.question: How many rounds with two winners for rename_claim?

steps.description: rename claim: rounds with two winners = 0. Atomic rename prevents double claims.
